discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms: theoretical proposals and the experimental realization of programmable atomic quantum matter

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Cirac and Zoller showed how to control and engineer many-body quantum systems built from atoms and light. Their work includes the trapped-ion quantum gate (1995) and the proposal, with Jaksch and colleagues, to realize Hubbard models with cold atoms in optical lattices (1998). Bloch's experiments, starting with the observation of the superfluid–Mott insulator transition (2002), turned these ideas into a new experimental field. Strongly correlated quantum matter could now be prepared, controlled and imaged one atom at a time. Together their work founded analog quantum simulation, as Feynman had envisioned it. It gave condensed-matter physics a clean, tunable laboratory and established the conceptual and technical basis for today's neutral-atom and ion-based quantum processors. These platforms are now used worldwide to study quantum magnetism, topological phases, thermalization and error-corrected quantum computation. This rare pairing of deep theoretical insight with landmark experiments has reshaped both many-body physics and quantum information science.
